newsitem.title: CANADA: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --
CANADA, Feb 24 - Montreal, QUE. - All terminals working normally, with no delays expected.

HONDURAS, Feb 24 - Puerto Cortes - Only one out of three tugs owned by the port authorities is working normally. One has been out of order for a year, 1 is working with only one engine. Four vessels berthed of which 1 loading zinc concentrates, 3 discharging (1 corn, 1 soya, 1 fertiliser). 2 Vessels anchored of which 1 in ballast, 1 to load lumber. 17 Vessels due of which 1 passenger, 8 to discharge/load containers/general cargo. 6 To load (5 bananas, 1 lumber). 2 To discharge (1 fertiliser, 1 lpg). No berthing delays expected.

MEXICO, Feb 25 - All ports working normally. Altamira - Four vessels in port of which 3 containers, 1 machinery. Tampico - Seven vessels in port of which 1 scrap, 3 general cargo, 1 sugar, 2 steel coils. Veracruz - 14 Vessels in port of which 2 containers, 2 general cargo, 2 pipes, 1 minerals, 2 grain, 2 sugar, 2 oil tankers, 1 vessel under repair. Manzanillo - 10 Vessels in port of which 3 general cargo, 3 containers, 4 grain. Coatzacoalcos - 20 Vessels in port of which 9 oil tankers, 10 chemicals, 1 vessel under repair.

PANAMA, Feb 24 - Balboa - Three vessels in port of which 1 bulker, 1 fishing vessel, 1 tanker. Istobal - Four vessels in port of which 2 container carriers, 1 tanker, 1 ro-ro. Panama Canal - Transit booking system normal and working at full capacity. Position 24/2 - 44 Vessels due, 22 in queue, 13 booked, 41 due. 23/2 - Actual arrivals 41, transits 44, average of booked and non-booked canal waters time 23.6 hours.

UNITED STATES, Feb 24 - Hampton Roads, Va - Five general cargo/container vessels berthed and operating, 1 at anchor, 1 bulker berthed loading coal, 1 bulker loading grain, 1 tanker discharging crude oil, 1 bulker lightering salt. 8 Vessels berthed under repair and/or layberth. Honolulu, Hi - Honolulu harbour - 3 Container vessels, 2 tugs and barges berthed. Honolulu anchorage - 2 Vessels for bunkers, 1 tanker awaiting berth. Barbers Point harbour - 1 Vessel discharging coal, 1 loading scrap metal. Offpoint moorings - 1 Tanker discharging crude oil.

East Coast - Baltimore, Md - No congestion expected at Dundalk terminal this week. Clear Candd canal/Baltimore harbour low ceiling. Elevators and coal operations working normally, with no delays. Consol Coal - Average waiting time 5 days. Liquid bulk facilities working normally, no berthing congestion. Anchorage available at Baltimore and Annapolis. Charleston, Sc - Container terminals expect light traffic this week. Oil facilities expect moderate traffic for the early part of the week, but no delays expted. Jacksonville, Fl - No congestion/delays for Jacksonville or Fernandina Beach, Fl. Miami, Fl - No congestion at container or gantry berths. Ro-ro berths vacant all week. Passenger terminals will be in full operation. New York, Ny - No congestion at anchorages or at container and tanker terminals. Sugar terminals congested.

Norfolk, Va - Southern Coal pier - Scheduled maintenance to No. 1 ship loading system from 8-29/4, during this period the ship loader will be out of service. 18 Vessels due this week, 2 anchored waiting to load. Dominion terminal - 12 Vessels due, 1 anchored waiting to load. Pier IX coal terminal - 5 Vessels due during the week. Cargill - 1 Vessel due this week. Container and general cargo terminals working normally with no delays. Oil and bulk terminals all working normally. All channels open and ice free, with prevailing depths available. Philadelphia, Pa - No congestion at Philadelphia, Camden or Wilmington, no dredging,repairs/navigational problems.

Savannah, Ga - Garden city terminals expect a busy week, with heaviest congestion mid-week. Ocean terminals and east coast terminals also expect a busy week, but no congestion. Long delays expected at Colonial Marine terminals bulk clay facility. Savannah sugar refinery - 1 Vessel operating with a barge to follow. All liquid bulk facilities working normally, with no congestion expected. Navigation remain normal. Vessels may expect delays due to periods of fog.

GULF COAST - Houston, Tx - City docks - Congested until 3/3. For the past two days, the channel has closed at night and reopened in late morning due to fog. No congestion at public elevator. Cargill elevator and farmland grain elevator. Galveston. New Orleans, La - Seasonal rain causing delays, especially to grain loaders. River stage at 12.9 ft. And expected to go up. Normal transit times expected. Bar pilots advise that draft for Mississippi River Gulf outlet will be 36 ft. The present max permissible draft at S.W. Pass is 47 ft. Fw. for vessels under 100,000 dwt and 46 ft. Fw. for vessels over 100,000 dwt. Due to an accident at the Zennoh elevator (Mile 168.3), loading operations for both grain and wood-chips have been suspended. Damage appears substantial.

WEST COAST - Columbia river - 17 Grain vessels in port at present of which 6 loading and 11 waiting, average waiting period 3-5 days. Coos Bay, Or - Last week normal, however the end of the month appears to be very busy. One log vessel is due to load at Ocean terminal and 1 wood-chip vessel is loading at Oregon chip terminal. Liner-board vessels are due to load at Coos Bay dock and another lumber and a nickel vessel are due next week. Honolulu, Hi - Traffic average for next week, no delays expected for offport anchorages or import berths, assuming normal weather.

Long Beach, Ca - Metropolitan (lb-212-214) - Moderate for March, with berthing delays of 1-2 days expected. Koch Carbon (lb-211 1 vessel due for March, no berthing delays expected. Kaiser (la-49) - Moderate for March (coal,petcoke), 1-2 days berthing delay expected. March looks moderate in Los Angeles/Long Beach harbour for bulk cargoes. San Francisco, Ca - Anchorages open, but still a shoaling problem at Stockton. Pilots are taking vessels with max. 28 ft. Fw. drafts. Army corps. carrying out emergency dredging and the channel should be open towards the beginning of March. The bagged rice season is winding down with only 1-2 vessels remaining. Seattle, Wa - Both grain elevators have a back log of vessels anchored awaiting berths.
